Name: Hemoglobin
What_It_Is: The protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen around your body.
If_High: Can be seen with dehydration, living at high altitude, smoking, or conditions that make the body produce extra red cells.
If_Low: Often points to anaemia, which can come from low iron, low vitamin B12 or folate, blood loss, or chronic illness. It can cause tiredness and breathlessness.
Range_Source: ABIM Jan 2026 (upper limits); WHO 2011 anaemia cut-offs (lower limits 13 / 12); urgent thresholds team-chosen, not source-verified

Name: RBC count
Aliases: rbc|rbc count|total rbc count|red blood cell count|red blood cells|erythrocytes
What_It_Is: The number of red blood cells in your blood.
If_High: Can be seen with dehydration or when the body makes extra red cells.
If_Low: Often goes along with anaemia or blood loss.

Name: Hematocrit (PCV)
What_It_Is: The share of your blood volume that is made up of red blood cells.
If_High: Often rises with dehydration.
If_Low: Often goes along with anaemia.

Name: MCV
What_It_Is: The average size of your red blood cells.
If_High: Large red cells can be seen with low vitamin B12 or folate, thyroid problems, or alcohol use.
If_Low: Small red cells are commonly seen with iron deficiency or thalassemia trait.

Name: MCH
What_It_Is: The average amount of haemoglobin inside each red blood cell.
If_High: Often goes with larger red cells.
If_Low: Often goes with iron deficiency.

Name: MCHC
What_It_Is: How concentrated haemoglobin is inside red blood cells.
If_High: Rarely meaningful on its own.
If_Low: Often goes with iron deficiency.

Name: RDW
What_It_Is: How much your red blood cells vary in size.
If_High: Red cells of mixed sizes, often seen early in iron, B12 or folate deficiency.
If_Low: Usually not significant.

Name: WBC (white cell count)
Aliases: wbc|wbc count|total wbc count|total leucocyte count|total leukocyte count|tlc|white blood cell count|white blood cells|leucocytes
What_It_Is: The total number of white blood cells that fight infection.
If_High: Commonly rises with infections, inflammation, stress or steroid use.
If_Low: Can be seen after viral infections, with some medicines, or when bone marrow is under strain.
Range_Source: ABIM Jan 2026; urgent thresholds team-chosen, not source-verified

Name: Neutrophils
What_It_Is: The most common white blood cell. They respond first to bacterial infections.
If_High: Commonly raised with bacterial infection or stress.
If_Low: Can follow viral infections or some medicines.
Range_Source: Derived from ABIM: segmented neutrophils 50-70 plus bands 0-5

Name: Lymphocytes
What_It_Is: White blood cells that fight viruses and help immunity.
If_High: Commonly raised after viral infections.
If_Low: Can be seen with stress, steroids or some infections.

Name: Eosinophils
What_It_Is: White blood cells involved in allergies and parasite infections.
If_High: Commonly raised with allergies, asthma or parasitic infections.
If_Low: Usually not significant.

Name: Monocytes
What_It_Is: White blood cells that clean up germs and damaged cells.
If_High: Can be raised during recovery from infection or with chronic inflammation.
If_Low: Usually not significant.

Name: Basophils
What_It_Is: A rare white blood cell involved in allergic reactions.
If_High: Rarely raised; worth discussing with a doctor if persistently high.
If_Low: Usually not significant.

Name: Platelets
What_It_Is: Tiny cell fragments that help your blood clot.
If_High: Can be raised with iron deficiency, infection or inflammation.
If_Low: Can be seen with viral infections such as dengue, some medicines, or immune conditions. Very low counts raise bleeding risk.
Range_Source: ABIM Jan 2026; urgent thresholds team-chosen, not source-verified

Name: ESR
What_It_Is: A general marker of inflammation in the body.
If_High: Rises with infection, inflammation, anaemia and in pregnancy. It does not point to one specific cause.
If_Low: Usually not significant.

Name: Fasting glucose
Aliases: fasting glucose|fasting blood sugar|fasting blood glucose|glucose fasting|glucose - fasting|glucose (fasting)|fbs|fbg|blood sugar fasting|blood sugar (fasting)|blood glucose fasting
What_It_Is: Your blood sugar after at least 8 hours without food.
If_High: 100 to 125 is the pre-diabetes range and 126 or more on repeat testing suggests diabetes.
If_Low: Low sugar can cause shakiness, sweating and confusion; it can be linked to skipped meals or diabetes medicines.
Range_Source: ABIM Jan 2026; ADA Standards 2026 (prediabetes 100-125, diabetes >=126); urgent thresholds team-chosen, not source-verified

Name: Post-meal glucose
Aliases: post prandial glucose|postprandial glucose|post prandial blood sugar|postprandial blood sugar|pp blood sugar|ppbs|ppbg|glucose pp|glucose - pp|glucose (pp)
What_It_Is: Your blood sugar about 2 hours after a meal.
If_High: 140 to 199 is the pre-diabetes range and 200 or more suggests diabetes.
If_Low: Low sugar after meals is uncommon and worth discussing with a doctor.
Range_Source: ADA Standards 2026 (2-h OGTT: <140 normal, 140-199 prediabetes, >=200 diabetes); applied to post-meal values as an approximation; urgent thresholds team-chosen, not source-verified

Name: Random glucose
Aliases: random glucose|random blood sugar|rbs|glucose random|glucose - random
What_It_Is: Your blood sugar at a random time of day.
If_High: 200 or more with symptoms suggests diabetes.
If_Low: Low sugar can cause shakiness, sweating and confusion.
Range_Source: Team-chosen; no reference-range source (ADA gives only the >=200 diagnostic value with symptoms); urgent thresholds team-chosen, not source-verified

Name: HbA1c
Aliases: hba1c|hb a1c|hemoglobin a1c|haemoglobin a1c|glycosylated hemoglobin|glycosylated haemoglobin|glycated hemoglobin|glycated haemoglobin|a1c
What_It_Is: Your average blood sugar over roughly the last 3 months.
If_High: 5.7 to 6.4 is the pre-diabetes range and 6.5 or more suggests diabetes.
If_Low: Usually not a concern; can be affected by anaemia or recent blood loss.
Range_Source: ABIM Jan 2026; ADA Standards 2026 (5.7-6.4 prediabetes, >=6.5 diabetes)

Name: Total cholesterol
What_It_Is: All the cholesterol carried in your blood.
If_High: Raises long-term risk of heart disease and stroke, especially with high LDL.
If_Low: Rarely a concern, though very low levels can have other causes.

Name: LDL cholesterol
Aliases: ldl cholesterol|ldl|ldl-c|ldl chol|ldl cholesterol direct|ldl cholesterol - direct|ldl cholesterol (calculated)
What_It_Is: The "bad" cholesterol that can build up in artery walls.
If_High: Raises risk of heart disease and stroke.
If_Low: Rarely a concern.

Name: HDL cholesterol
Aliases: hdl cholesterol|hdl|hdl-c|hdl chol|hdl cholesterol direct|hdl cholesterol - direct
What_It_Is: The "good" cholesterol that helps clear other cholesterol from your blood.
If_High: Higher is usually protective.
If_Low: Low HDL raises heart disease risk. Exercise, not smoking and healthy fats can help.
Range_Source: ABIM Jan 2026 (low: male <40, female <50); upper limit 100 team-chosen

Name: Triglycerides
What_It_Is: A type of fat in your blood that comes from food and is made by your liver.
If_High: Often linked to sugary or fatty food, alcohol, excess weight, diabetes or an underactive thyroid. Very high levels can inflame the pancreas.
If_Low: Rarely a concern.

Name: VLDL cholesterol
What_It_Is: A fat-carrying particle made by the liver. It usually tracks triglycerides.
If_High: Usually rises together with triglycerides.
If_Low: Rarely a concern.
Range_Source: Derived: Friedewald VLDL = triglycerides / 5, so normal triglycerides (<150) give <30; not listed by ABIM

Name: Creatinine
What_It_Is: A waste product from muscle that your kidneys filter out.
If_High: May mean the kidneys are filtering less well. Dehydration, heavy exercise, high-protein diet or some medicines can also raise it.
If_Low: Usually not a concern; can be seen with low muscle mass.
Range_Source: ABIM Jan 2026; urgent thresholds team-chosen, not source-verified

Name: Urea
What_It_Is: A waste product of protein breakdown that your kidneys remove.
If_High: Can be raised with dehydration, high-protein diet or reduced kidney function.
If_Low: Can be seen with low protein intake or liver disease.
Range_Source: Derived from ABIM BUN 8-20 mg/dL x 2.14; urea itself is not listed by ABIM

Name: BUN
What_It_Is: The nitrogen part of urea in your blood; another kidney waste marker.
If_High: Can be raised with dehydration or reduced kidney function.
If_Low: Can be seen with low protein intake or liver disease.

Name: Uric acid
What_It_Is: A by-product of breaking down purines in food and body cells.
If_High: High levels can cause gout and kidney stones. Red meat, alcohol and some medicines can raise it.
If_Low: Usually not a concern.

Name: Sodium
What_It_Is: An electrolyte that balances fluids and supports nerves and muscles.
If_High: Often a sign of dehydration.
If_Low: Can come from too much water intake, some medicines or heart, kidney or liver conditions. Severe lows are an emergency.
Range_Source: ABIM Jan 2026; urgent thresholds team-chosen, not source-verified

Name: Potassium
What_It_Is: An electrolyte vital for heart rhythm and muscle function.
If_High: Can affect heart rhythm; may come from kidney problems or some medicines.
If_Low: Can come from vomiting, diarrhoea or water tablets and may cause weakness or cramps.
Range_Source: ABIM Jan 2026; urgent thresholds team-chosen, not source-verified

Name: Chloride
What_It_Is: An electrolyte that works with sodium to balance body fluids.
If_High: Often follows dehydration.
If_Low: Often follows vomiting or fluid loss.

Name: Calcium
What_It_Is: A mineral essential for bones, muscles and nerves.
If_High: May be caused by overactive parathyroid glands, excess vitamin D or some cancers.
If_Low: Often linked to low vitamin D, low albumin or parathyroid issues.
Range_Source: ABIM Jan 2026; urgent thresholds team-chosen, not source-verified

Name: Phosphorus
What_It_Is: A mineral that works with calcium to keep bones strong.
If_High: Often related to kidney problems.
If_Low: Can come from poor nutrition or low vitamin D.

Name: Magnesium
What_It_Is: A mineral that supports muscles, nerves and heart rhythm.
If_High: Usually related to kidney problems or supplements.
If_Low: Can come from poor intake, alcohol, diarrhoea or some medicines.

Name: Total bilirubin
What_It_Is: A yellow pigment made when old red blood cells break down; the liver clears it.
If_High: Can cause yellowing of skin and eyes (jaundice). May be linked to liver, bile duct or red cell breakdown issues.
If_Low: Usually not a concern.

Name: Direct bilirubin
What_It_Is: Bilirubin that the liver has already processed.
If_High: Often points to a liver or bile duct problem.
If_Low: Usually not a concern.

Name: SGOT (AST)
What_It_Is: An enzyme found in the liver, heart and muscles.
If_High: Raised with liver inflammation, alcohol, fatty liver, some medicines, or after heavy exercise or muscle injury.
If_Low: Usually not significant.

Name: SGPT (ALT)
What_It_Is: An enzyme mostly found in the liver. It is a more liver-specific marker than SGOT.
If_High: Raised with fatty liver, hepatitis, alcohol, some medicines or supplements.
If_Low: Usually not significant.

Name: Alkaline phosphatase (ALP)
What_It_Is: An enzyme found in the liver, bile ducts and bones.
If_High: Can come from liver or bile duct problems, bone conditions, or growth in children and teenagers.
If_Low: Can be seen with zinc deficiency or some rare conditions.

Name: GGT
Aliases: ggt|gamma gt|gamma glutamyl transferase|gamma-glutamyl transferase|gamma glutamyl transpeptidase
What_It_Is: A liver and bile duct enzyme, very sensitive to alcohol and some medicines.
If_High: Raised with alcohol use, fatty liver, bile duct problems or some medicines.
If_Low: Usually not significant.

Name: Total protein
Aliases: total protein|protein total|serum protein|serum total protein
What_It_Is: The sum of albumin and globulin proteins in your blood.
If_High: Can occur with dehydration or chronic inflammation.
If_Low: Can come from poor nutrition, liver or kidney disease.

Name: Albumin
What_It_Is: The main protein made by the liver; it keeps fluid inside blood vessels.
If_High: Usually due to dehydration.
If_Low: Can come from poor nutrition, liver disease or kidney protein loss.

Name: Globulin
What_It_Is: Proteins that include antibodies and carriers.
If_High: Can occur with chronic infection or inflammation.
If_Low: Can occur with weak immunity or poor nutrition.

Name: TSH
What_It_Is: A hormone from the brain that tells your thyroid how much hormone to make.
If_High: Suggests an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism); symptoms can include tiredness, weight gain and feeling cold.
If_Low: Suggests an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism); symptoms can include palpitations, weight loss and feeling hot.

Name: Total T3
What_It_Is: An active thyroid hormone.
If_High: Can go with an overactive thyroid.
If_Low: Can go with an underactive thyroid or illness.

Name: Total T4
What_It_Is: The main hormone made by the thyroid gland.
If_High: Can go with an overactive thyroid.
If_Low: Can go with an underactive thyroid.

Name: Free T4
What_It_Is: The active, unbound part of thyroxine.
If_High: Can go with an overactive thyroid.
If_Low: Can go with an underactive thyroid.

Name: Vitamin D (25-OH)
Aliases: vitamin d|25-oh vitamin d|25 oh vitamin d|vitamin d3|25-hydroxy vitamin d|25 hydroxy vitamin d|vitamin d total|vitamin d (25-oh)
What_It_Is: Helps your body absorb calcium for strong bones; made in skin with sunlight.
If_High: Too much is usually from over-supplementation and can raise calcium.
If_Low: Very common in India. The 2011 Endocrine Society guideline called below 20 ng/mL deficiency and 21 to 29 insufficiency (a 2024 update moved away from fixed cut-offs). Can cause bone pain and weakness.

Name: Vitamin B12
What_It_Is: Needed to make red blood cells and keep nerves healthy.
If_High: Often from supplements; rarely a concern.
If_Low: Common in vegetarians and with some stomach conditions or medicines. Can cause tiredness, tingling and anaemia.

Name: Folate
What_It_Is: A B vitamin needed to make DNA and red blood cells.
If_High: Usually from supplements.
If_Low: Can come from poor diet or alcohol; leads to anaemia.

Name: Ferritin
What_It_Is: Shows how much iron your body has stored.
If_High: Can be raised in inflammation, liver disease or iron overload.
If_Low: The earliest sign of iron deficiency.

Name: Serum iron
What_It_Is: The amount of iron circulating in your blood.
If_High: Can occur after taking iron supplements or with iron overload.
If_Low: Suggests iron deficiency or chronic illness.

Name: TIBC
What_It_Is: How much iron your blood can carry.
If_High: Rises when the body is short of iron.
If_Low: Can be seen with inflammation or malnutrition.

Name: Transferrin saturation
What_It_Is: The percentage of iron-carrying protein that is filled with iron.
If_High: May suggest iron overload.
If_Low: Suggests iron deficiency.

Name: CRP
What_It_Is: A marker that rises quickly with inflammation or infection.
If_High: Suggests inflammation or infection somewhere in the body.
If_Low: Not significant.
